<h2><a id="numbers"></a>When to use digits or words</h2>
<p>Numbers written as digits are generally easier to read and understand.</p>
<p>When writing numbers, use:</p>
<ul>
<li>digits for numbers 2 and above</li>
<li>words for numbers ‘zero’ and ‘one’.</li>
</ul>
<p>The numbers ‘0’ and ‘1’ are difficult for some users to read. Some typefaces make it hard to distinguish between the digits ‘0’ and ‘1’ and letters such as ‘o’, ‘l’ or ‘7’. Writing ‘zero’ and ‘one’ reduces the risk of confusion.</p>
<h3>Exceptions</h3>
<p>There are situations where writing numbers as words improves readability, while in other cases digits provide greater clarity or precision.</p>
<p>The choice depends on the context, the audience and how easily the information can be understood.</p>
<div class="accordion-toggle inline-accordion">
<div class="accordion-trigger">
<span class="accordion-title">
<button type="button" class="accordion-toggle__btn" lang="en-NZ" hidden="">Expand all
</button>
</span>
</div>
</div>


<details class="accordion-item inline-accordion expander-type-accordion heading-h4">
<summary class="accordion-item-button accordion-trigger" data-ga-event="click" data-ga-category="In-page accordion" data-ga-action="When to use words" data-ga-label="/home">
<h4>



<span class="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></span>


<span class="accordion-title">When to use words</span>




</h4>
</summary>
<div hidden="until-found" class="accordion-content">
<p>Use words instead of digits when:</p>
<ul>
<li>starting a sentence or heading (unless it’s a year)</li>
<li>writing a fraction</li>
<li>the number is part of the official name of a person, place, organisation or thing</li>
<li>quoting a figure of speech</li>
<li>presenting content that follows a style that spells out numbers from one to nine (for example, to maintain the journalistic style in a media release).</li>
</ul>
</div>
</details>



<details class="accordion-item inline-accordion expander-type-accordion heading-h4">
<summary class="accordion-item-button accordion-trigger" data-ga-event="click" data-ga-category="In-page accordion" data-ga-action="When to use digits" data-ga-label="/home">
<h4>



<span class="accordion-icon" aria-hidden="true"></span>


<span class="accordion-title">When to use digits</span>




</h4>
</summary>
<div hidden="until-found" class="accordion-content">
<p>Always use digits, even for ‘zero’ and ‘one’, when writing:</p>
<ul>
<li>age, dates, times and units of measurement</li>
<li>percentages (unless they're at the start of a sentence)</li>
<li>decimals, numerical comparison and mathematical relationships</li>
<li>structured data such as lists, tables and charts</li>
<li>scientific or technical content.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</details>

<div class="callout-example">
<figure class="fig-example" aria-label="Examples of writing numbers as digits or words" role="figure">
<figcaption id="fig-example-figcaption-1">Examples of writing numbers as digits or words</figcaption>
<ul>
<li>Your child must be 5 years old.</li>
<li>The report includes 3 recommendations.</li>
<li>The target is zero emissions.</li>
<li>Measles is one of the most contagious diseases.</li>
<li>One of the 3 options is to apply online.</li>
<li>Five actions to make change.</li>
<li>2020 is the year of the horse.</li>
<li>State Highway 1 is closed due to a crash.</li>
<li>A picture is worth a thousand words.</li>
<li>One-third of the participants completed the survey.</li>
<li>About 1 in 6 New Zealanders are disabled.</li>
<li>Around 25% of all waste is sent to landfill.</li>
<li>The route is 50km long.</li>
</ul>
</figure>
</div>
<h3>Big numbers</h3>
<p>When writing large numbers:</p>
<ul>
<li>use commas to separate thousands when the number is over 999</li>
<li>combine a number with the word ‘million’ for figures over 999,999 — unless the number needs to be written in full (for example, in technical data)</li>
<li>do not abbreviate ‘million’ as ‘m’.</li>
</ul>
<p>Apply the same approach for ‘billion’, ‘trillion’ and so on.</p>
<div class="callout-example">
<figure class="fig-example" aria-label="Examples of writing big numbers" role="figure">
<figcaption id="fig-example-figcaption-1">Examples of writing big numbers</figcaption>
<ul>
<li>1,000 days (not a thousand days)</li>
<li>5.31 million (not 5,313,900)</li>
</ul>
</figure>
</div>
<h3>Ordinal numbers</h3>
<p>Ordinal numbers indicate the order or position of something — such as first, second or third.</p>
<ul>
<li>Write ordinal numbers from first to ninth as words.</li>
<li>Use digits with a suffix from 10th and above.</li>
</ul>
<h4>Exceptions to using words for ordinal numbers</h4>
<ul>
<li>Do not use ordinals in dates.</li>
<li>Centuries always use digits, even under 10.</li>
</ul>
<div class="callout-example">
<figure class="fig-example" aria-label="Examples of writing ordinals" role="figure">
<figcaption id="fig-example-figcaption-1">Examples of writing ordinals</figcaption>
<ul>
<li>Second referendum (not 2nd referendum)</li>
<li>7 July (not 7th July)</li>
<li>9th century (not ninth century)</li>
</ul>
</figure>
</div>
<h2><a id="datesandtimes"></a>Dates and times</h2>
<ul>
<li>Write dates as day, month and year in full.</li>
<li>Do not use ordinal numbers, for example, 1st or 3rd, in dates.</li>
<li>Show time using a 12-hour clock.</li>
<li>Show start and end times in full.</li>
<li>Use ‘midnight’ not ‘00:00’.</li>
<li>Spell out the names of days and months in full.</li>
<li>Use ‘to’ instead of an en dash (–) in date and time ranges as it’s easier for screen readers to read out.</li>
</ul>
<div class="callout-example">
<figure class="fig-example" aria-label="Examples of writing dates and times" role="figure">
<figcaption id="fig-example-figcaption-1">Examples of writing dates and times</figcaption>
<ul>
<li>12 noon (not 12pm)</li>
<li>5:30pm (not 17:30hrs)</li>
<li>10am to 11am (not 10 to 11am)</li>
<li>Monday to Friday</li>
<li>2 March 2020</li>
<li>Tuesday 8 July 2025</li>
<li>Monday 21 September to Friday 2 October</li>
<li>10 November to 21 December 2026</li>
</ul>
</figure>
</div>
<h2><a id="phone"></a>Phone numbers</h2>
<ul>
<li>Always use ‘freephone’ (not phone) for numbers that are free to call, such as an 0800 number.</li>
<li>If it’s a New Zealand freephone, always put ‘(NZ only)’ after the number.</li>
<li>Use cellphone, rather than cell-phone or cell phone.</li>
<li>Use ‘TTY’ as the label for any number that provides a text service for the deaf community.</li>
<li>Unless they’re used in the middle of a sentence, 'phone' and 'freephone' should always have a colon after them.</li>
</ul>
<div class="callout-example">
<figure class="fig-example" aria-label="Examples of writing phone numbers" role="figure">
<figcaption id="fig-example-figcaption-1">Examples of writing phone numbers</figcaption>
<ul>
<li>Phone: +64 4 456 2390</li>
<li>Freephone: 0800 611 116 (NZ only)</li>
<li>TTY: 0800 111 113</li>
<li>Call a registered nurse on Healthline, freephone 0800 611 116.</li>
</ul>
</figure>
</div>
<h3>HTML code for phone numbers</h3>
<ul>
<li>Mark up phone numbers as links so people can tap or click to call.</li>
<li>Use a non-breaking space to separate parts of a telephone number. This keeps the number together on one line.</li>
</ul>
<div class="callout-example">
<figure class="fig-example" aria-label="Examples of HTML code for phone numbers" role="figure">
<figcaption id="fig-example-figcaption-1">Examples of HTML code for phone numbers</figcaption>
<pre>&lt;a href="tel:+64045558080"&gt;04 555 8080&lt;/a&gt;</pre>
<pre>&lt;a href="tel:+64034447777"&gt;+64 03 444 7777&lt;/a&gt;</pre>
<pre>&lt;a href="tel:0800555222"&gt;0800 555 222&lt;/a&gt;</pre>
</figure>
</div>
<h2><a id="currency"></a>Currency</h2>
<p>Where the content is only talking about New Zealand dollars, use ‘$’. If users could be confused about the currency being referenced, use NZD$.</p>
<p>For other currencies, use the country prefix followed by the relevant symbol for that currency.</p>
<div class="callout-example">
<figure class="fig-example" aria-label="Examples of writing currency" role="figure">
<figcaption id="fig-example-figcaption-1">Examples of writing currency</figcaption>
<ul>
<li>The adult minimum wage in New Zealand is $23.95 per hour.</li>
<li>The fee for international applicants is NZD$100.</li>
<li>If you’re a United States citizen, you pay USD$640.</li>
<li>If you’re an Australian citizen, it costs AUD$890.</li>
<li>British citizens pay GBP£420.</li>
<li>Japanese citizens pay JPY¥550.</li>
</ul>
</figure>
</div>
